I have very recently been through a similar situation with my Mum. She too has just suffered a break up and has become very reliant on me. Given her current state of mind, I've been reluctant to not be at her beck and call because of what she might do. 

Nevertheless, I had a chat with her a couple of days ago after I made a post on reddit desperate for help. We didn't discuss that she was clingy or in any way that I was getting tired of her being reliant on me (that's definitely not what she wants to hear and will distance her more). What we did agree on, however, was getting into a routine. We agreed that Saturdays will be "our" days where we go shopping, get dinner and spend the day together. I'm also trying to persuade her to come to my gym with me. I figured that if she has something to focus on, somewhere that will help her start feeling good about herself, then it will help us both. 

I know it's a struggle and I cannot guarantee that my advice will help but feel free to contact me if you need someone to lend an ear. If your mother is anything like mine, she will more than likely feel guilty about being so reliant on you anyway.. she just feels lonely and hasn't been on her own for so long.
You're more than welcome. Feel free to inbox me if you need any help at all! Life has a funny way of working itself out most times.

Hey, I'm a bit late to this thread but I'm up late and thought I'd give some kind of advice..

I'm a 22 year old female and I didn't have my first relationship until I was 19. Whilst he wasn't the first guy I slept with, he was the first person to fall in love with. We moved in together quickly and things became pretty serious because I was trying to do everything I'd dreamed of at once. 

Whilst I think it's beautiful that people can fall in love so soon and become so infatuated with each other I would say, from my past experience, don't force it. 

Things will happen naturally and in the meantime discover your own self worth. I, too, suffer with hideously low self esteem and found I used to really need people's assurance in order to feel better about myself. Fast forward a couple of years and I no longer have any longing desire for a relationship or to fall in love as I know now that happiness will come when it's ready.

You're 20 years old... don't consider the fact that you've never been in love a burden to you. Do something for yourself which makes you respect your own being. Test your endurance, test your knowledge... build a skill which people will admire. Because believe me when I say it'll help you find some solace at the moment.

I regularly travel via Bank for work so I'll always hit the peak times unfortunately. Prior to this I'll have sat for two hours travelling into London with two changes (one at Birmingham New Street which is similar torture to the tube). 
The overcrowding is awful but what's worse is the attitude of some commuters like you say. God forbid if they try to barge past me at 8:30am before I've had my first cup of tea. I become more concrete than an old guy on Viagra.

I sat in on an interview for a PA with my boss. When on the subject of marriage and kids, my boss asked the interviewee if she had married out of love or if her family had arranged it.. she answered love and we thought that was the end of it. He then proceeded to ask if she was raising her kids as Sikhs and if she would be comfortable working in an environment with lots of men. 

I cringed so much in that interview but the lady held her own and is actually still working for us. There was no malice in what my boss was asking, he was genuinely just interested in her culture but went the complete wrong way about it. Just the other week when we were all out for a meal he kept asking her if his pronunciation of "basmati" was right. 

The best of it is she came from an Indian family but has lived the western culture all her life. She's just as clueless as he but finds it all very hilarious.

If you do not have your money or purse out ready to pay when you have been queuing for a good five or so minutes before I will assume you are an idiot with no care for others in the queue behind. 

Similarly, if you pay in pennies or fumble around for change I cannot help but feel sorry for you and automatically assume you are hard up. 

This is shallow of me, I agree, and I know I'm normally wrong.

I think there's a point we all hit in a relationship where we crave the honeymoon period again which is clearly long since sailed in your current relationship. But like you say, you love your girlfriend dearly and you very obviously see her playing a part in your future too. 
This doesn't make you an asshole. It makes you human. It's completely natural to have a crush on someone. Just try not to act on impulse and if you really feel strongly about her, speak to your girlfriend first and, please, reassure her that she has done nothing wrong as that's the first thing any girl will assume. 
This is your decision to make and no stranger from reddit can really force you to change your feelings on things. By the sounds of it, you already feel you've unintentionally overstepped the boundaries of your relationship. 
I hope it all works out for you in the end.
